name: Architectural faience
summary: A hollow slab of fine clay with a coloured glaze on the visible face. It clads a wall with a bright, washable skin.
how: Press or cast the slab hollow, 30 to 60 mm thick, with ribs on the back.
Fire the slab to a biscuit at about 1050 °C.
Spray the visible face with a coloured glaze and fire it again.
Tie the slab to the frame with metal ties and set it with thin joints.

origin.note: English works make glazed architectural faience for shops, pubs and public buildings.

adoptions.via: New York and Los Angeles works make glazed slabs in blue-green, cream and gold for Art Deco towers and cinemas.
